subject: NimbusCloud SLA addendum: performance commitments & evidence request
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@nimbuscloud.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nimbuscloud.com
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NimbusCloud SLA addendum: performance commitments & evidence request

Hi Lauren / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward finalizing the MSA + order form, our procurement and cloud reliability teams have a few asks tied to the availability and latency commitments in the SOW. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the following as an addendum to the MSA?

High-level asks from my side (procurement + reliability):
- Availability: 99.95% uptime for production API endpoints across our primary region (us-west-2) with a clearly defined credit schedule.
- Latency: P95 <= 300ms for inference calls for the standard LLM SKU under normal load; carveouts for traffic spikes documented.
- Evidence: telemetry/telemetry retention details (metrics, sample traces), incident timeline examples, and an evidence matrix mapping how credits are calculated.
- Order form language: a short exhibit we can attach to the order form describing the scope (endpoints, excluded maintenance windows, and regional failover).

Procurement would like an editable redline (Word) for the addendum and an evidence matrix we can attach to the SOW. Are you able to provide a first draft and a DocuSign routing plan? Our target signing window is the week of July 8.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Ethan Cole
Senior Procurement Manager | NimbusCloud

Ethan — thanks for laying this out so clearly. We can accommodate a tailored SLA addendum; sending an initial execution playbook and an editable draft for the addendum attached. Highlights up front: 

- Availability: we can propose a 99.95% production uptime target scoped to the API endpoints called out in the order form. We will include automatic regional fallback language (secondary region) and an explicit maintenance window carveout.
- Latency: P95 target language will be included for the standard inference SKU; we'll add a definition for "normal load" and an attachment describing stress/burst carveouts.
- Credits: I attached a proposed credit schedule tied to monthly uptime percentage and a short example calculation.
- Evidence matrix: attached workbook includes the telemetry fields we can share and suggested retention periods (metrics, traces, audit logs).

Next steps / asks for NimbusCloud: 
1) Please review the attached redline (Nimbus_SLA_Redline_20280620.docx) and mark any commercial/legal items.
2) Confirm whether the retention windows (metrics: 90 days; traces: 30 days; audit logs: 1 year) meet your compliance needs.
3) When you're ready, indicate the preferred DocuSign routing and approvers so we can prepare the envelope.

I've looped in Marissa from Ops for the telemetry and Karthik from Legal/Contracts for order form language. If you want to escalate availability tolerances, call out the expected annual request volume so we can model cost/thresholds.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx; evidence_matrix_nimbus.xlsx; Nimbus_SLA_Redline_20280620.docx

Thanks — Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Adding a quick ops note on telemetry / evidence.

- We can provide a CSV export (sample) for monthly uptime calculation and a short runbook that maps outage types to credit triggers.

Lauren / Marissa — thank you, this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from procurement/engineering after a brief review of the draft: 

- The proposed credit schedule looks reasonable as a starting point, but procurement will ask Legal to tighten language around calculation windows (calendar month vs rolling 30 days). Can you propose both options in the redline?
- For latency: the P95 definition in your draft references "standard inference SKU". Can you add an explicit SKU identifier and confirm whether quantized variants are in/out of scope?
- Evidence: procurement will want the sample telemetry file and the runbook before the DocuSign envelope — that helps us validate the credit formula.

We prefer DocuSign routing as: 1) NimbusCloud PO approver (Procurement) 2) NimbusCloud Legal 3) Redwood Legal 4) Redwood Sales exec. Target: envelope ready by July 1 so we can route internally and sign the week of July 8 as discussed.

I'll review the redline and return consolidated comments by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Ethan

Ethan — quick legal/contract note and proposed order form language snippet to expedite review: 

Legal notes: 
- We'll include both calculation-window options (calendar month and rolling 30-day) in the addendum and call out the customer's selection in the order form.
- Canary/rollback language: suggest we add a short operational fallback clause that allows Redwood to perform staged rollouts with automatic rollback if latency degradation >30% from baseline for a sustained 15-minute window; this protects both parties during upgrades.

Order form exhibit snippet (editable):
"Exhibit X — Performance Commitments":
- Scope: Applies to endpoints listed in the Order Form. Excluded activities: scheduled maintenance, agreed maintenance windows, force majeure, and customer-caused disruptions.
- Availability: Production API endpoints shall maintain monthly availability of 99.95% (subject to selected calculation-window). See attached credit schedule.
- Latency: Measured P95 across successful inference API responses for SKU: RW-STD-8 (standard inference). Quantized model variants (SKU: RW-STD-Q4) are considered a separate SKU and are out of scope unless explicitly listed in the Order Form.

Next steps from our side: 
1) Kimberly will prepare a redline with both calculation-window options and the SKU definitions.
2) Marissa will upload the sample telemetry export and a 30-day baseline report by EOD June 22.
3) Lauren will confirm DocuSign routing and prepare the envelope for July 1.

Kimberly / Marissa — please proceed. Ethan — look for the redline and evidence matrix shortly.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
